panels.rationale: Single-image figure: grayscale ultrasound of a neonate (article title: 'Proximal Ureteral Atresia in a Caribbean Neonate With Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney') showing a large cystic lesion in the region of the right kidney marked by a black arrow and the on-image text 'CYSTIC LESION' (10.17 cm). The disease-focused article title plus the panel-specific captioned manifestation (cystic lesion of the right kidney with multiple septations, left kidney structurally normal) supports attribution to multicystic dysplastic kidney. The appearance is a large septated cystic mass rather than the textbook cluster of multiple non-communicating cysts, hence 'variant' and moderate confidence; no skin is visible so skin tone is null and ethnicity is not explicitly stated in the caption or in-text mentions.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 8 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H). A: Ultrasound image of right kidney showing cystic changes and increased echogenicity, consistent with early stages of MCDK. B: Ultrasound image of right kidney showing cystic changes and increased echogenicity, consistent with early stages of MCDK. C: Ultrasound showing ureteral dilatation associated with MCDK presentation. D: Sagittal ultrasound of right flank demonstrating classic features of MCDK, including noncommunicating cysts and cystic replacement of the kidney. E: Ultrasound of a crossed fused left kidney showing increased parenchymal echogenicity in the context of a urological complex. F: Ultrasound showing ureteral ectopy/dilation, consistent with associated urological findings in this case. G: Transverse ultrasound of the left ureter showing dilatation and displacement. H: Sagittal ultrasound of the right ureter showing dilation consistent with atresia/agenesis.

panels.figure_caption: Abdomen US, day 0 of life (a)–(c). (a) and (b) sagittal images, solitary right kidney: cysts in the upper pole, increased renal parenchymal echogenicity, and mild dilatation of the renal pelvis (arrow); (c) right parasagittal image, bladder: mild dilatation of the right ureter extending to the ureterovesical junction (arrow). Abdomen US, 6 months of age (d)–(h). (d) sagittal image, right flank: noncommunicating cysts with no intervening renal parenchyma consistent with a right multicystic dysplastic kidney (arrow) and moderate hydronephrosis of the inferior crossed fused left kidney; (e) sagittal image shows increased renal parenchymal echogenicity of the crossed fused left kidney with relative preservation of parenchymal thickness (arrow); (f) sagittal image shows moderate dilatation of the proximal left ureter to the right of midline consistent with crossed fused ectopy; (g) transverse image, bladder: dilated distal left ureter confirms the crossed fused left renal ectopy; (h) sagittal image, bladder: dilated tapered atretic right ureter.
in_text_mentions: crotia, bilateral external auditory canal stenosis, and a single umbilical artery. Screening abdomen ultrasound (US) at day 0 of life demonstrated a solitary kidney on the right with multiple noncommunicating cysts in the upper pole, giving the appearance of a segmental MCDK. The US showed renal pelvis prominence and a mildly dilated ureter extending to the UVJ (Figure 1). The left renal fossa was empty. Echocardiographic evaluation revealed atrial and ventricular septal defects. The infant was discharged home on prophylactic antibiotics and was scheduled for follow-up in an outpatient clinic.

in_text_mentions: that the right kidney measured 11.5 cm with no cysts. Left kidney measured 14.2 cm (enlarged and irregular) and consisted of multiple noncommunicating thin walled cysts that are distributed randomly (Figure 1). No normal renal tissue is apparent on ultrasound. A CT scan of abdominal and pelvis without contrast revealed that the right kidney was normal and not hypertrophic. Left kidney appeared to be grossly abnormal to the point it was described to look as a large hydronephrotic sac with multiple non communicating dilated cystic spaces, but no actual hydronephrosis, left ureteropelvic junction
